### About

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b750896-e00e-4357-966d-b4fff2539008

Related:
- [Reddit: Remove outer indentation with mini.indentscope](https://www.reddit.com/r/neovim/comments/1i8eyyq/remove_outer_indentation_with_miniindentscope)
- [Neovim discussions: Show and Tell](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/discussions/34221)

### Unscope

The most useful use case here is unscoping (deleting around a scope, `dS`). If you want to keep your config lightweight, just change your keymap to this:

```lua
vim.keymap.set("n", "grs", function() -- dS
  vim.cmd("sil norm " .. string.rep("[i", vim.v.count - 1) .. "viiy']vaiopgv<")
end, { desc = "Unscope" })
```

### All-in

Since Neovim doesn’t support multi-cursor editing or multiple independent selections, we can’t just select a range and let an operator handle everything at once. Each operation has to be implemented separately.

<details><summary>Version 1</summary>

```lua
vim.keymap.set("o", "S", function()
  if not vim.list_contains({ "d", "c", "y", "g@" }, vim.v.operator) then
    return
  end

  local scope = MiniIndentscope.get_scope(nil, math.huge)
  for _ = 2, vim.v.count1 do
    scope = MiniIndentscope.get_scope(scope.border.top, math.huge)
  end

  if scope.border.indent < 0 then
    return
  end

  local change = function(from, to, with)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, from - 1, to, false, with)
  end

  local dedent = function(from, to)
    local count = scope.body.indent - scope.border.indent
    local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, from - 1, to, false)
    for i, ln in ipairs(lines) do
      local indent
      indent = vim.fn.indent(from - 1 + i)
      indent = math.max(0, indent - count)
      lines[i] = vim.text.indent(indent, ln, { expandtab = 1 })
    end
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, from - 1, to, false, lines)
  end

  local select = function(from, to)
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { from, 0 })
    vim.cmd("norm! V")
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { to, 0 })
  end

  local border, body = scope.border, scope.body
  local inner_lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, body.top - 1, body.bottom, false)

  if vim.list_contains({ "y", "d", "c" }, vim.v.operator) then
    local copy = {}
    vim.list_extend(copy, vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, border.top - 1, body.top - 1, false))
    vim.list_extend(copy, vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, body.bottom, border.bottom, false))
    -- NOTE: `setreg` doesn't work inside `vim.keymap.set("o")`
    vim.schedule(function()
      vim.fn.setreg(vim.v.register, table.concat(copy, "\n"), "l")
    end)
  end

  if vim.v.operator == "y" then
    return
  end

  if vim.v.operator == "d" then
    change(border.top, border.bottom, inner_lines)
    dedent(border.top, border.top + #inner_lines - 1)
    -- HACK: defer cursor to avoid visual selection
    vim.schedule(function()
      MiniIndentscope.move_cursor("top", true, scope)
    end)
  end

  if vim.v.operator == "c" then
    table.insert(inner_lines, 1, "")
    change(border.top, border.bottom, inner_lines)
    dedent(border.top + 1, border.top + #inner_lines - 1)
    select(border.top, body.top - 1)
  end

  if vim.v.operator == "g@" then
    require("vim._comment").toggle_lines(border.top, body.top - 1)
    require("vim._comment").toggle_lines(body.bottom + 1, border.bottom)
  end
end, { desc = "Border scope operator" })
```

</details>

<details open><summary>Version 2 (+fixes)</summary>

```lua
vim.keymap.set("o", "S", function()
  if not vim.list_contains({ "d", "c", "y", "g@" }, vim.v.operator) then
    return
  end
  if vim.v.operator == 'g@' and not vim.o.operatorfunc:find("vim._comment") then
    return
  end

  local scope = MiniIndentscope.get_scope(nil, math.huge)
  for _ = 2, vim.v.count1 do
    scope = MiniIndentscope.get_scope(scope.border.top, math.huge)
  end
  if scope.border.indent < 0 then
    return
  end

  local change = function(from, to, with)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, from - 1, to, false, with)
  end
  local dedent = function(from, to)
    vim.cmd(string.format('silent %s,%s <', from, to))
  end
  local cursor = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)
  local select = function(from, to)
    if from == false then
      vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, cursor)
      return
    end
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { from, 0 })
    vim.cmd [[norm! V]]
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { to, 0 })
  end

  local border, body = scope.border, scope.body
  local inner_lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, body.top - 1, body.bottom, false)

  if vim.v.operator == "g@" then
    require("vim._comment").toggle_lines(border.top, body.top - 1)
    require("vim._comment").toggle_lines(body.bottom + 1, border.bottom)
    return
  end

  if vim.list_contains({ "y", "d", "c" }, vim.v.operator) then
    local copy = {}
    vim.list_extend(copy, vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, border.top - 1, body.top - 1, false))
    vim.list_extend(copy, vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, body.bottom, border.bottom, false))
    -- NOTE: `setreg` doesn't work inside `vim.keymap.set("o")`
    vim.schedule(function()
      vim.fn.setreg(vim.v.register, table.concat(copy, "\n"), "l")
    end)
  end
  if vim.v.operator == "y" then
    return
  end

  if vim.v.operator == "d" then
    change(border.top, border.bottom, inner_lines)
    dedent(border.top, border.top + #inner_lines - 1)
    select(false)
    -- HACK: defer cursor to avoid visual selection
    vim.schedule(function()
      MiniIndentscope.move_cursor("top", true, scope)
    end)
  end

  if vim.v.operator == "c" then
    table.insert(inner_lines, 1, "")
    change(border.top, border.bottom, inner_lines)
    dedent(border.top + 1, border.top + #inner_lines - 1)
    select(border.top, body.top - 1)
  end
end, { desc = "Border scope textobject" })
```

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for sharing. There are couple of issues I noticed:
- The `dedent` function will force replace tab indentation into spaces. This is usually a big issue. An alternative is to manually compute target indent space based on the actual leading whitespace. Or use `:<` command (as [done in 'mini.surround'](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/5d938b3a078a7eeae23ba9f04f180066ab8bd9ef/lua/mini/surround.lua#L2090-L2093)).
- The `vim.v.operator == "g@"` check is true for *any* custom operator, not only `gc`. One way to hard-code the action only for specific operator is to [check 'operatorfunc'](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/5d938b3a078a7eeae23ba9f04f180066ab8bd9ef/lua/mini/ai.lua#L1094-L1095), but that might be brittle.
- The "o" (Operator-pending) mode mappings do not represent operators. They are motions (acts from cursor to some place; usually also work in Normal and Visual mode) or textobjects (computes and selects a region regardless of the cursor position). So the better description is "Border scope textobjet".

reply_data.body:
Honestly, I only use it for unscoping (`dS`), so rather than having such a long keymap, it makes more sense to keep it simple:

```lua
vim.keymap.set("n", "grs", function()
  vim.cmd("sil norm " .. string.rep("[i", vim.v.count - 1) .. "viiy']vaiopgv<")
end , {})
```

I also tried using an `expr` keymap, but it triggers highlighting with `vim.hl.on_yank()` and internally respects `v:count`, which can be a bit misleading in this case.
